title: Corner: 15-Minute Discovery Call Script
summary: The discovery call happens before the live demo. This script qualifies the prospect, uncovers their #1 pain point, and books the 30-minute demo. Every demo starts here.
content:
Corner: 15-Minute Discovery Call Script

For: Patrik (runs before every demo) Duration: 15 minutes max. Hard stop. Goal: Qualify the prospect. Find the pain. Book the demo. Pre-requisite: You know their name and business. That's it.

This call IS the audit. At the end, you have two outcomes: (1) demo booked, or (2) they're not a fit and you saved both of you 30 minutes. Both are wins.

BEFORE THE CALL (2 min)

Pull up a notes doc. Write their name and business at the top. You're going to fill in:

  • Team size
  • Their #1 time drain
  • Current AI/tools usage
  • Their definition of "worth it"

You need these for the demo. Without them, the demo is generic. Generic demos don't close.

MINUTE 0-2: FRAME IT

(Don't sell. Set the context.)

"Hey [Name], thanks for getting on. I'm going to keep this tight -- 15 minutes. I want to understand your business a bit before I show you anything. That way when I do show you Corner, it's actually relevant to what you're dealing with -- not just a generic walkthrough."

"Sound good?"

Let them say yes. Then:

"Perfect. Just a few questions and we'll go from there."

MINUTE 2-8: THE AUDIT QUESTIONS

Ask exactly these four. In this order. Don't skip any. Don't add more.

Q1: "Tell me about your team -- how many people, and what does a typical week look like for you personally?"

What you're listening for: solo operator vs real team, whether Patrik is doing tasks that should be delegated, energy around the question (tired = good fit, fine = dig deeper)

Q2: "What's the one thing eating the most of your time that shouldn't be?"

This is the money question. Write down their exact words. You'll use them in the demo. If they say "following up with leads" -- in the demo you show the Follow-Up agent first. If they say "my calendar is a disaster" -- you show the Scheduler agent. Personalization = conversion.

If they say "I don't know" or "everything" -- ask: "If you could give one thing to someone else tomorrow, what would it be?"

Q3: "Are you using any AI tools right now -- ChatGPT, Zapier, anything like that?"

What you're listening for: sophistication level. If they use ChatGPT daily, they understand the category. If they've "heard about AI but haven't tried it" -- frame Corner as the guided version, not the DIY version. Adjust your demo language accordingly.

Q4: "Last one. What would have to be true for you to say this was worth the investment at 6 months?"

This is the close setup. They're telling you exactly what the bar is. Write it down. At minute 25 of the demo, you read it back to them and show how Corner hits it.

MINUTE 8-12: QUALIFY + TEASE

By now you know if they're a fit. If they are:

"Everything you just described -- [repeat their exact words from Q2 back to them] -- that's exactly what Corner was built for."

"Here's what I want to do. I'm going to show you how AOM actually runs its business on Corner. Not slides, not screenshots -- our real operations. You'll see [specific agent that matches their pain] doing exactly what you described."

"It takes about 30 minutes and I think you'll leave knowing whether this is for you or not."

"What does your calendar look like this week?"

MINUTE 12-15: BOOK THE DEMO

Do not end this call without a day and time on the calendar.

When they give you availability: "Perfect. I'll send a calendar invite right now. I'll have Corner pulled up and ready when we get on."

Send the invite before you hang up. Seriously -- send it while they're still on the call. Invite acceptance rate drops by 40% if you send it more than 30 minutes later.

IF THEY'RE NOT A FIT

Signs they're not a fit:

  • Solo operator with no employees (no one to delegate to, no workflow to systematize)
  • Under $200k revenue (can't afford $3,500/month)
  • They want to "try it themselves" with no hand-holding (wrong product)

How to exit gracefully:

"Honestly, based on what you've told me, I think you'd get more value from [ChatGPT / Notion / a freelancer] right now. Corner is designed for businesses with a real ops layer -- once you've got the team and the volume, it becomes a multiplier. Come back to me in 6 months and let's have this conversation again."

They'll remember you were honest. Referrals come from prospects you turned away with integrity.

AFTER THE CALL (5 min)

Fill in your notes:

  • Team size: ___
  • Their #1 pain: ___ (exact words)
  • Current AI usage: ___
  • Their definition of worth it: ___
  • Demo booked: YES / NO

Before the demo, re-read these notes and decide:

  • Which agent do you show FIRST? (matches their pain point)
  • Which line do you read back to them in minute 25? (their Q4 answer)
  • What language level do they use? (adjust tech depth in demo)

Without this, the demo is a generic walkthrough. With it, it feels like you built Corner for them specifically. That's why deals close.
